topics.title: Reserve Bank of India Act 1934
topics.hook: The Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 is a critical part of the Indian economy.
topics.story: The Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 plays a pivotal role in shaping the financial landscape. It impacts borrowing, lending, and overall market liquidity. Understanding its mechanism is essential for comprehending macroeconomic stability in India. Its implications stretch across various sectors, affecting both public and private entities. For decades, it has been a subject of intense policy debate and legislative reform, reflecting the evolving nature of the Indian economy and its integration with global markets. Policymakers continually adjust their approach to balance growth with stability.

passages.title: Passage 1
passages.passage: This passage covers key economic indicators and institutional frameworks relevant to the Indian economy. The central bank employs various instruments to manage liquidity. Concurrently, the government uses fiscal policy to direct growth. Regulatory bodies like SEBI and IRDAI ensure market integrity. The transition from the Planning Commission to NITI Aayog reflects a shift towards cooperative federalism. Meanwhile, the IBC and SARFAESI acts have transformed the resolution of non-performing assets. The introduction of GST unified the indirect tax regime. Finally, the balance of payments dictates the country's external sector resilience.
